notes:
Separate snapshot reading deadlines from human draft/review use. Successful, in-window, latest-batch snapshots remain available for draft generation, editing and approval after the original read/result expiry. Their source revision, observed time and provenance stay immutable; draft eligibility is derived from request input lineage, not by extending persisted TTLs. Failed/missing/cross-scope/superseded/input-changed or first-delivered-after-deadline evidence never becomes draft-ready. The UI explicitly labels draft usability and snapshot age rather than calling old evidence current site state.

Human execution confirmations only request another outbound read when required snapshots are strictly older than 24 hours, or their observed timestamps are missing/invalid. The age comes from the oldest required actual observedAt, not receipt/request-update times. Fresh evidence proceeds without another prepare job. Rechecks that observe changed versions/original values/required conditions fail closed and require re-generation/review; incomplete rechecks are bounded and never issue authorization. The confirmation and authorization transactions recheck age and evidence identity, while the runner and Bridge keep their write-time original-value/version/capability guards. Confirmation tokens, write authorization and execution leases keep their independent short lifetimes. Automatic standing-authorization execution retains its original strict freshness gates; private preview body and attachment retention are not relaxed.

No migration, no historical row rewrite, no environment/bootstrap change. Compatible with the sealed production runner 0.9.1: the earlier uncommitted runner TTL patch is not shipped here. Rolling back to v0.2.30 application images needs no data action; it restores the older stricter snapshot-age behavior. No manual worker/dispatcher stop is needed for this migration-free update.

Test-first evidence: unit policy module absent and old generation refresh behavior failed before implementation; disposable PostgreSQL draft/review and execution-age cases ran red before the changes. Final main-tree validation: 2179 API tests passed, 198 skipped, zero failed (includes 48 uncommitted WordPress tests excluded from this release); three-package typecheck zero errors; disposable PostgreSQL16 migrations twice, six suites 141/141 including real Python runner payload controls; focused unit tests 127/127; real components/synthetic HTTP browser checks 14/14 at 1440 and 375px, including old draft readiness, invalid-input refusal and confirmation never writing; existing runner guard tests 60/60; history pages 173/173 and actual report-to-latest-content navigation passed. Clean committed-source CI-order verification is separately recorded before tagging. Full production snapshot draft usability is checked read-only after upgrade, never inferred from local tests.
